messages.content:
Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.


Claimed finding status: missing

Finding rationale:
Section 11 addresses term, breach termination and survival (including a run-off right for existing Customers and continuing support), but nowhere requires Commerce One to provide transition assistance or to return our and our Customers' data. The only post-termination data provision is the mutual Confidential Information return/destroy obligation in Section 11.3, which is not a data export right (no format, no timing, no machine-readable requirement) and gives Commerce One a destruction option over material it holds. Because Commerce One hosts the MarketSite.net Service accessed by Corio and its Customers (Section 2.6), data resides on Commerce One's systems, so an exit path is needed. Inserted Section 11.4 to match the playbook preferred position: up to six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, machine-readable data return within thirty days, then deletion with written certification; fallback of 90 days' assistance offered in the comment.

Original paragraphs:
p0098: 11.3 Effect of Termination. The following Sections shall survive the termination or expiration of this Agreement for any reason: 4.2, 5.3, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12 and 14. Corio's right to allow its then-existing Customers and their Software Users to use and access the Software in accordance with Section 2 of this Agreement and all payment obligations related thereto shall survive any termination or expiration of this Agreement. Commerce One's obligation to provide Software support and maintenance to Corio and its Customers shall survive any termination or expiration of this Agreement, provided Corio continues to make its annual support and maintenance payments as specified in this Agreement. Upon termination or expiration of this Agreement, each party shall otherwise return or destroy any Confidential Information of the other party provided, however, Corio may retain any Confidential Information necessary for Corio to continue supporting it's then-existing Customers.

Resolved definitions:
COMMERCE ONE: This License and Hosting Agreement (the "AGREEMENT") is made and entered into as of October 29, 1999 ("EFFECTIVE DATE") by and between Corio Inc., a Delaware corporation, having its principal place of business at 700 Bay Road, Suite 210, Redwood City, CA 94063 ("CORIO") and Commerce One, Inc., a Delaware corporation having its principal place of business at 1600 Rivera Avenue, Walnut Creek, CA 94596 ("COMMERCE ONE").
SOFTWARE USER: 1.1 "SOFTWARE USER" means a named user of the Corio Services worldwide to whom a user identification number and password has been assigned, which permits that user to access and use the Software on a designated Corio Server. The identification number and password used by a Software User is reusable and reassignable and may be used and transferred by Corio, in accordance with the licenses granted below, between Customers as one Customer discontinues the Corio Services and another Customer subscribes.
SOFTWARE: 1.10 "SOFTWARE" means Commerce One's proprietary software described in EXHIBIT A attached hereto and made a part hereof, in object code form only, and any Updates or Upgrades (as defined below) thereto.

Rendered redline:
p0098: 11.3 Effect of Termination. The following Sections shall survive the termination or expiration of this Agreement for any reason: 4.2, 5.3, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12 and 14. Corio's right to allow its then-existing Customers and their Software Users to use and access the Software in accordance with Section 2 of this Agreement and all payment obligations related thereto shall survive any termination or expiration of this Agreement. Commerce One's obligation to provide Software support and maintenance to Corio and its Customers shall survive any termination or expiration of this Agreement, provided Corio continues to make its annual support and maintenance payments as specified in this Agreement. Upon termination or expiration of this Agreement, each party shall otherwise return or destroy any Confidential Information of the other party provided, however, Corio may retain any Confidential Information necessary for Corio to continue supporting it's then-existing Customers.
11.4 Transition Assistance and Data Return. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Commerce One shall (a) at Corio's request, provide reasonable transition assistance to Corio and its Customers for up to six (6) months at Commerce One's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days of Corio's request, return to Corio all data of Corio and its Customers in Commerce One's possession or control, including data stored or processed in connection with the Software or the MarketSite.net Service, in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete such data from its systems and certify such deletion to Corio in writing. This Section 11.4 shall survive any termination or expiration of this Agreement.

Comment:
[Playbook] We added a transition-assistance and data-return provision: on expiry or termination Commerce One provides up to six months of assistance at its then-current rates, returns our and our Customers' data in a machine-readable format within thirty days, and then deletes and certifies deletion. Our playbook requires an orderly exit path, particularly where our Customers' data sits in the MarketSite.net Service; we can live with a 90-day assistance period if six months is unworkable.

reasons: Deviation is correctly identified: the express product warranty runs only 60 days from the Effective Date with a hard December 31, 1999 sunset — shorter than both the 12-month preferred and 90-day fallback positions — and there is no professional/workmanlike warranty for the Section 5 installation, implementation, support, training and professional services.

Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

input.quote: MarketSite.net Access Fee: Due upon Software Acceptance, and on each annual anniversary of Software Acceptance thereafter.
input.rationale: There is no express take-or-pay, shortfall penalty or user-volume cap on Corio (Software Users are "Unlimited" and the revenue share is transaction/revenue-based; the only "minimum" references are drafting floors and the mutual audit true-up in 4.4). However, the MarketSite.net access fee is a fixed annual charge due on each anniversary (Exhibit B pricing "Year 1 [*] Year 2-5, and beyond: [*]") across a five-year initial term that Corio can only exit for breach or insolvency (11.1/11.2), with no right to reduce or discontinue access. That is effectively a multi-year commitment without an exit, contrary to our position that fees be payable only for services used or ordered. Because the annual access fee is the agreed commercial structure, we take the fallback: a 30 days' notice right to reduce or discontinue MarketSite.net access with a pro-rata true-up rather than a penalty.

Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.

Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

input.rationale: There is no express take-or-pay, shortfall penalty or user-volume cap on Corio (Software Users are "Unlimited" and the revenue share is transaction/revenue-based; the only "minimum" references are drafting floors and the mutual audit true-up in 4.4). However, the MarketSite.net access fee is a fixed annual charge due on each anniversary (Exhibit B pricing "Year 1 [*] Year 2-5, and beyond: [*]") across a five-year initial term that Corio can only exit for breach or insolvency (11.1/11.2), with no right to reduce or discontinue access. That is effectively a multi-year commitment without an exit, contrary to our position that fees be payable only for services used or ordered. Because the annual access fee is the agreed commercial structure, we take the fallback: a 30 days' notice right to reduce or discontinue MarketSite.net access with a pro-rata true-up rather than a penalty.

**Finding submitted: deviation (medium), confidence 0.58**

What I checked and found:
- **No classic take-or-pay:** no "commit to purchase," no shortfall penalty on us, no volume cap — Exhibit B lists Software Users as "Unlimited" (p0151), and the revenue share we pay is a percentage of actual Application Management Revenue (p0157). The "minimum limitation of 40 Authorized Software Users per Customer" (p0158) is a qualifier on the free 3,000-user allowance, not a purchase minimum. Section 4.4's "shortfall" is a mutual audit true-up, which is acceptable.
- **The real exposure:** the MarketSite.net access fee is a fixed annual charge due on each anniversary (p0168; pricing "Year 2-5, and beyond" at p0153) across a five-year initial term terminable only for breach or insolvency (11.1/11.2). That is a multi-year fee commitment with no reduction or exit right.

Redline (validated, `ok:true`): a minimal proviso in the Exhibit B payment terms letting Corio discontinue or reduce MarketSite.net access on 30 days' notice, with a pro-rata true-up and no penalty or shortfall charge — our fallback position, since the annual access fee itself is the agreed commercial structure.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
There is no express take-or-pay, shortfall penalty or user-volume cap on Corio (Software Users are "Unlimited" and the revenue share is transaction/revenue-based; the only "minimum" references are drafting floors and the mutual audit true-up in 4.4). However, the MarketSite.net access fee is a fixed annual charge due on each anniversary (Exhibit B pricing "Year 1 [*] Year 2-5, and beyond: [*]") across a five-year initial term that Corio can only exit for breach or insolvency (11.1/11.2), with no right to reduce or discontinue access. That is effectively a multi-year commitment without an exit, contrary to our position that fees be payable only for services used or ordered. Because the annual access fee is the agreed commercial structure, we take the fallback: a 30 days' notice right to reduce or discontinue MarketSite.net access with a pro-rata true-up rather than a penalty.

Original paragraphs:
p0168: MarketSite.net Access Fee: Due upon Software Acceptance, and on each annual anniversary of Software Acceptance thereafter.
p0096: 11.1 Term. The term of this Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and shall continue in full force and effect for an initial period of five (5) years. Thereafter, this Agreement shall automatically renew for subsequent one (1) year periods unless either party provides the other party with written notification at least thirty (30) days prior to the expiration of the initial five (5) year term or any one (1) year renewal thereof of its intention to terminate this Agreement.
p0153: MARKETSITE.NET SERVICE FEES: MarketSite.net Service Access: Year 1 [*] Year 2-5, and beyond: [*]

Resolved definitions:
SOFTWARE: 1.10 "SOFTWARE" means Commerce One's proprietary software described in EXHIBIT A attached hereto and made a part hereof, in object code form only, and any Updates or Upgrades (as defined below) thereto.

Rendered redline:
p0168: MarketSite.net Access Fee: Due upon Software Acceptance, and on each annual anniversary of Software Acceptance thereafter; provided that Corio may discontinue or reduce its MarketSite.net Service access upon thirty (30) days' written notice to Commerce One, in which case no further MarketSite.net Access Fee shall accrue for the discontinued or reduced access and any prepaid fees shall be trued up and refunded on a pro rata basis, without penalty or shortfall charge.

Comment:
[Playbook] The MarketSite.net access fee recurs on every anniversary through the five-year initial term with no reduction or discontinuation right, which operates as a take-or-pay commitment. Our position is that fees should be payable only for services actually used or ordered, so we have added a 30 days' notice right to reduce or discontinue access with a pro-rata true-up rather than a penalty.

[{"id":"f-ip-598bd48e","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 13 SHARED RESOURCES.","rationale":"Section 13.5 correctly vests Developments (including software interface coding created solely by Corio) in Corio and includes a Commerce One assignment in the continuation at p0116, which matches our preferred position. Because the annual access fee is the agreed commercial structure, we take the fallback: a 30 days' notice right to reduce or discontinue MarketSite.net access with a pro-rata true-up rather than a penalty.","proposal":"Add a 30-day notice right for Corio to discontinue or reduce MarketSite.net access, with pro-rata true-up instead of continuing annual fees for the full five-year term.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-nosolicit-c948f1b5","ruleId":"NOSOLICIT","ruleTitle":"Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer","severity":"medium","status":"needs_review","sectionRef":"§ 13 SHARED RESOURCES.","rationale":"Compliant with the preferred position (\"No non-solicit on Customer\"): the Agreement contains no non-solicitation, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant, so no redline or counterparty comment is proposed. {"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.5 (Commerce One / Corio Agreement)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side — Corio)

## Executive summary
